newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania central bank to take deposits from banks.
newsitem.headline: Romania central bank to take deposits from banks.

text.p: Romania's government has issued a decree allowing the central bank (BNR) to take deposits from commercial banks.
The government said on Thursday the BNR was allowed to negotiate and pay interest for such operations but gave no details.

Local bankers said the decree sought to improve the management of the money market, allowing the BNR to start pilot open-market operations in the absence of more sophisticated tools to regulate leu liquidity.
BNR officials were unavailable for comment. The decree becomes effective after publication in the Official Gazette.
In recent months, the BNR has soaked up dollar excesses after large foreign inflows to prevent the leu currency from appreciating and to keep exports competitive.
The BNR's dollar purchases fueled leu liquidity and with few tools to mop up excess leu funds, money market rates have fallen rapidly to around 60 percent from 190 in April.
Money market dealers have urged the BNR to act to drain leu liquidity or risk undermining its tight monetary policy meant to fight soaring inflation.
Central bank governor Mugur Isarescu said last week there was a need to diversify liquidity management instruments to be added to the BNR's limited government securities portfolio.
Romania tightened monetary policy earlier this year to combat rising inflation after liberalising the foreign exchange market and freeing fuel, energy and food prices.
Monthly inflation slowed to 6.9 percent in April from a record 30.7 percent in March and the government aims to cut it to about two percent by the end of the year.
